lessons.correction: Increase economy and technology. Strengthen ground forces. Increase defense. Maintain expansion. Continue production.
lessons.mistake: Over-committing to offense before your defense is solid, potentially leaving you vulnerable to a ground attack.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you see more of the opponent's army composition or if they apply pressure.
lessons.title: Stabilize before pushing
lessons.when: Early-midgame, around 240 seconds, with heavy defense and moderate economy, while the opponent shows a ground posture with Marine cues.
lessons.why: The opponent's ground posture suggests a potential ground attack. Stabilizing your defense while developing your economy and tech is prudent.

lessons.correction: Increase economy and technology. Strengthen ground forces. Increase defense. Maintain expansion. Continue production.
lessons.mistake: Over-committing to offense before your defense is solid, risking vulnerability when the opponent's intentions are unclear.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you observe more of the opponent's army composition or production structures, or when you reach a new tech milestone.
lessons.title: Balanced development under uncertainty
lessons.when: Early-midgame, around 300-360 seconds, with heavy defense and moderate economy, while the opponent's posture is unknown.
lessons.why: With limited information, balanced development keeps options open. Strengthening ground forces provides a solid base for any transition.

lessons.correction: Increase economy, production, and technology. Strengthen ground forces. Maintain defense and expansion. Continue air development.
lessons.mistake: Neglecting ground defense, leaving you vulnerable to drops or flanking maneuvers.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you see more of the opponent's army composition or if they expand further.
lessons.title: Maintain ground defense against drops
lessons.when: Late-midgame, around 600 seconds, with heavy economy and production, while the opponent shows a ground posture with SiegeTank, Reaper, Thor, and Medivac.
lessons.why: The opponent's ground posture suggests a potential ground attack. Strengthening ground forces and maintaining defense is prudent while continuing development.
